model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the annual area of vineyards (in thousands of hectares) across seven countries — Spain, France, China/Continental, Italy, Turkey, the USA, and Argentina — from 2013 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the years, while the vertical axis shows the area in “Хиляди хектари” (thousands of hectares), ranging from 0 to 1200 with tick marks at intervals of 200. Each year features a grouped set of seven colored bars, corresponding to the countries listed in the legend: Spain (dark blue), France (orange), China/Continental (gray), Italy (yellow), Turkey (light blue), USA (green), and Argentina (dark navy). Spain consistently maintains the largest vineyard area throughout the period, with values hovering around 950–1000 thousand hectares. France follows with approximately 750–800 thousand hectares, while China/Continental and Italy show similar levels, fluctuating between 700 and 800 thousand hectares. Turkey, the USA, and Argentina have significantly smaller areas, with Turkey around 400–450, the USA around 400–450, and Argentina consistently near 200–220 thousand hectares. No bars are shaded or emphasized, and the data appears to be presented in chronological order without sorting by magnitude. The chart provides a clear visual comparison of vineyard sizes across these major wine-producing nations over a decade.
